You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 594c11d0e1d445f580898a2b8c850f2e3f099368 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Corey Minyard <corey@minyard.net>
Date: Tue, 27 Jan 2026 07:22:35 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] ipmi: Fix use-after-free and list corruption on sender error

The analysis from Breno:

When the SMI sender returns an error, smi_work() delivers an error
response but then jumps back to restart without cleaning up properly:

1. intf->curr_msg is not cleared, so no new message is pulled
2. newmsg still points to the message, causing sender() to be called
   again with the same message
3. If sender() fails again, deliver_err_response() is called with
   the same recv_msg that was already queued for delivery

This causes list_add corruption ("list_add double add") because the
recv_msg is added to the user_msgs list twice. Subsequently, the
corrupted list leads to use-after-free when the memory is freed and
reused, and eventually a NULL pointer dereference when accessing
recv_msg->done.

The buggy sequence:

  sender() fails
    -> deliver_err_response(recv_msg)  // recv_msg queued for delivery
    -> goto restart                    // curr_msg not cleared!
  sender() fails again (same message!)
    -> deliver_err_response(recv_msg)  // tries to queue same recv_msg
    -> LIST CORRUPTION

Fix this by freeing the message and setting it to NULL on a send error.
Also, always free the newmsg on a send error, otherwise it will leak.

Reported-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/20260127-ipmi-v1-0-ba5cc90f516f@debian.org/
Fixes: 9cf93a8fa9513 ("ipmi: Allow an SMI sender to return an error")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 4.18
Reviewed-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Signed-off-by: Corey Minyard <corey@minyard.net>

diff --git a/drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c b/drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c
index 3f48fc6ab596..a590a67294e2 100644
--- a/drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c
+++ b/drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c
@@ -4852,8 +4852,15 @@ static void smi_work(struct work_struct *t)
 			if (newmsg->recv_msg)
 				deliver_err_response(intf,
 						     newmsg->recv_msg, cc);
-			else
-				ipmi_free_smi_msg(newmsg);
+			if (!run_to_completion)
+				spin_lock_irqsave(&intf->xmit_msgs_lock,
+						  flags);
+			intf->curr_msg = NULL;
+			if (!run_to_completion)
+				spin_unlock_irqrestore(&intf->xmit_msgs_lock,
+						       flags);
+			ipmi_free_smi_msg(newmsg);
+			newmsg = NULL;
 			goto restart;
 		}
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c`, to fix a use-after-free and list corruption bug in the `smi_work()` function. The changes ensure proper cleanup after an SMI sender error.

### Modifications in `drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c`:
- **Error handling in `smi_work()`**: When `sender()` returns an error, the code now:
  - Unconditionally calls `ipmi_free_smi_msg(newmsg)` to free the message object (previously this only happened if `newmsg->recv_msg` was NULL; otherwise the message leaked).
  - Clears `intf->curr_msg` to `NULL` under the `xmit_msgs_lock` spinlock (or without locking in run-to-completion mode) so that the next iteration will pull a new message from the queue.
  - Sets `newmsg = NULL` to prevent the same `newmsg` from being used in a subsequent `goto restart`.
- These changes prevent the original buggy sequence where `curr_msg` remained set and `newmsg` still pointed to the freed message, causing the same message to be sent again and its `recv_msg` to be double-queued, leading to list corruption and use-after-free.

### Relationships between changes:
- All changes are within the same error-handling block and are interdependent: freeing `newmsg` and clearing `curr_msg` ensure that the state is reset properly, while setting `newmsg = NULL` avoids a dangling pointer. Together, they fix the resource leak (message not freed) and the logic error (reusing the same failed message), thus eliminating the double list add and subsequent use-after-free.
